message.content: Rust forbids holding two simultaneous mutable references to a value because its borrow checker enforces exclusive ownership, guaranteeing that only one piece of code can modify the data at any time and preventing overlapping mutable accesses that could corrupt memory or create race conditions. This rule stops undefined‑behaviour bugs such as data races, double writes, and inconsistent state that arise from aliased mutable references.
